learning_objective: 🎯 Shrink down to the subatomic level! Follow the historical timeline of how scientists discovered the hidden structure of atoms, from solid spheres to glowing electron clouds.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: नाभिक (The dense center of an atom)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron. He imagined the atom as a sphere of positive charge with tiny negative electrons stuck inside it, like seeds in a watermelon or raisins in a pudding.

Rutherford shot alpha particles at a super-thin sheet of gold foil. Most passed straight through, but a few bounced right back! He discovered that atoms are mostly empty space, with a tiny, dense, positively charged center called the Nucleus.
Niels Bohr improved the model by showing that electrons don't just float randomly; they orbit the nucleus in fixed, specific paths called 'shells' or 'energy levels' (like planets around the sun).
Protons (+) and Neutrons (no charge) live packed together in the nucleus and make up almost all the atom's mass. Electrons (-) are incredibly tiny, weigh almost nothing, and spin around the outside.
The Atomic Number (Z) is the number of Protons (this defines the element!). The Mass Number (A) is the total number of Protons + Neutrons combined.

fun_activity.title: 🏟️ The Stadium Atom
fun_activity.instructions: To understand how much of an atom is 'empty space', imagine the atom is the size of a giant cricket stadium. The nucleus would be the size of a single marble sitting in the very center of the pitch, and the electrons would be tiny gnats buzzing in the top bleachers!

exam_tips: 📌 You will likely be asked to describe Rutherford's experiment and its three major conclusions (mostly empty space, dense center, positive nucleus).
📌 Memorize the charges and relative masses: Proton (+1, mass 1u), Neutron (0, mass 1u), Electron (-1, mass almost 0).
📌 Number of neutrons = Mass Number (A) - Atomic Number (Z).
quick_recap: ⭐ Atoms are electrically neutral because the number of positive protons exactly equals the number of negative electrons.
⭐ James Chadwick discovered the neutron much later because it has no electrical charge, making it hard to detect.
⭐ The maximum number of electrons in a shell is given by the formula $2n^2$.
